I'm 69 years old, and I've been farming these fields since I was 19 — fifty years now. It's just me and my wife at home, our children work in Shijiazhuang and send a little money, but this 10.1 mu is still what we live on. We grow wheat and maize, always have. The maize is coming out of the ground now — I harvested about 450 kg per mu this year, decent but not great because July was too wet. Now I need to get the wheat in.

**Wheat this year:** I'll plant around October 10th. I know the old saying — if you plant before National Day, you get straw but no grain; if you plant after the 15th, you get grain but no straw. Around the 10th is my sweet spot. I buy improved wheat seed from the supply store, about 35 yuan per mu. I don't buy the most expensive new varieties — I stick with what I know, something that's been reliable for 3-4 years. 

For fertilizer, I put down base fertilizer before planting. I use about 40 kg of compound fertilizer (15-15-15) per mu — that's one bag for every two mu, roughly. I spread it by hand and then till it in. Come March, when the wheat is jointing, I look at the color. If it's yellowish, I topdress with about 15 kg of urea per mu. The extension agent says I should put more, maybe 20 kg urea, but fertilizer prices have gone up and I'm old — I don't need to chase the maximum yield, I need a stable yield without going broke. So total nitrogen is probably around 13-14 kg per mu. I get some phosphorus and potassium from the compound bag, about 6 kg each per mu.

Irrigation is always a calculation of money and my back. I have a tube well, but pumping costs electricity. For wheat, I irrigate three times: once in winter if there's no snow (to keep the seedlings from freezing), once at jointing in spring, and once at grain filling in May. I skip the planting irrigation if the soil is moist enough after maize harvest. Three times is what I can manage — moving those pipes gets harder every year.

For weeds, I spray herbicide once in early spring. I don't spray for disease unless I see something really bad — those fungicides are expensive and I'm not sure they pay off on my small plot.

**Maize next summer:** The wheat comes off in mid-June, and I have maybe a week to get maize in the ground. I hire a tractor with a no-till planter — I can't manage the turnaround myself anymore, and my neighbor has a machine. It costs me, but if you miss that window, the maize won't mature before frost. I buy hybrid maize seed every year — you can't save hybrid seed, everyone knows that. It's about 45 yuan per mu.

For maize fertilizer, I put down about 35 kg of compound fertilizer per mu at planting, then topdress with 15 kg of urea per mu when the plants are knee-high and starting to tassel — that's early August. Total nitrogen is about 12 kg per mu. 

Maize irrigation depends on the summer rains. Most years I irrigate twice: once after planting if June is dry, and once at flowering in early August if there's no rain. Some years the monsoon does the work for me. I pray for rain — it's cheaper than electricity.

Pesticides for maize: I usually spray herbicide once, and if I see armyworms or corn borers, I spray insecticide. But I don't do preventive spraying — I watch the fields and decide.

**Labor and machinery:** My wife and I do all the fertilizing by hand, move the irrigation pipes, and do the spraying. It's hard on my knees, but hiring labor is 120-150 yuan per day and we can't afford much. We hire a combine for wheat harvest (about 50 yuan per mu) and a machine for maize harvest (about 60 yuan per mu). We also hire the tractor for maize planting. Altogether we do about 30 days of family labor and hire help for about 10 days.

**Yields:** I'm hoping for about 400 kg per mu of wheat and 450 kg per mu of maize. If the weather is normal and I don't get sick, that should happen. Last year the spring drought cut the wheat back to 380 kg, so you never know.

**Money:** Seed will cost me about 800 yuan, fertilizer about 2,100 yuan, irrigation electricity about 400 yuan, pesticides about 300 yuan, and machinery hire about 1,400 yuan. Total around 5,000 yuan. That's a big chunk of our savings, but if I don't spend it, the yields drop and we eat into next year's money even faster. I'd rather put down a bit more fertilizer than risk a bad year — losing 100 kg per mu hurts more than saving 200 yuan on urea.
